status: bounded selected-source and read-only Gemian alias audit; cycle not admitted
selected_findings: The gen3 WLAN HIF maps 0x11000080 through 0x110000ff; its named DMA register accesses are offsets 0x00 through 0x58, including a channel-local reset at offset 0x0c.

The selected MT6797 DT assigns ten I2C DMA windows of 0x80 bytes from 0x11000100 through 0x110005ff. Selected CONFIG_OF I2C code maps each platform device's second resource; the non-OF computed +0x180 formula is not its active path.

Named UART DMA windows begin at 0x11000600 and BTIF windows at 0x11000a00. None of those named starts or I2C windows overlaps WLAN's 0x80-byte channel, although the AP-DMA parent spans 0x11000000 through 0x11000fff.
The gen2 WLAN source also names 0x11000080, but its MT6797 ahb_pdma.c is absent from the selected build log; the gen3 ahb_pdma.c is present.

CONFIG_MTK_CMDQ=y. The linked cmdq_device.c consumes a subsystem table naming ap_dma_base at 0x11000000; a bounded exact-literal and CMDQ_SUBSYS_AP_DMA source search found no specific selected command targeting WLAN's channel. This is not proof that dynamic commands cannot target it.
decision: Do not admit the next effect-bearing cycle on channel separation alone. Exclude or bound generic CMDQ access to the AP-DMA range and establish shared clock, CONSYS remap/protection and worker failure ownership in the exact candidate.
limits: This audit covers named source and DT paths, not every computed address, firmware master, DMA transaction or CMDQ job.
The Gemian binding observation does not prove a CMDQ command accessed AP-DMA and does not validate the compile-only candidate.
No AP-DMA register access, radio action or new mainline boot occurred.
